correctness.rationale: For real T:ℓ_p²→ℓ_p² and even integer p≥2, Q=∥T∥^p(x^p+y^p)−(ax+by)^p−(cx+dy)^p is a nonzero globally nonnegative homogeneous binary form of degree p unless T is a scalar multiple of an isometry. Every real projective zero has even multiplicity, including infinity in the reciprocal chart. Hence at most p/2 projective directions and at most p antipodal norm-attaining unit vectors. Independently expanded the p=4 example T(x,y)=(x+y,x−y): ∥T∥₄⁴=8 and Q=6(x²−y²)², so exactly four norming vectors (±2^(−1/4),±2^(−1/4)). All p-even bound is proved, but p≥6 sharpness is not asserted. The p=2 Hilbert subcase is classical.
